lagprotest

lagprotest extends the Procrustean randomization test (PROTEST) to ordered multivariate series. It scans Procrustes concordance between two configurations across candidate temporal lags, tests each lag by permutation, and returns the lag profile, the lag of maximal concordance (minimum m²) and per-observation Procrustes residuals.

Two permutation schemes are available:

  • permutation = "cyclic" (default): cyclic shifts of the full series, optionally with its time reversal, applied before lagging. This keeps temporal autocorrelation under the null and assumes the series spans complete cycles (e.g., 12 monthly samples of an annual cycle).
  • permutation = "free": free permutation of rows within the overlapping window, as in vegan::protest(). Rows are assumed exchangeable, which autocorrelated series violate; Type I error can be severely inflated.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("diogoprov/lagprotest")

Example 

library(lagprotest)

# Two 12-month series in which X leads Y by 2 months
sim <- simulate_lagged_series(n_times = 12, true_lag = 2, noise_sd = 0.5,
                              seed = 1)

fit <- lagged_protest(sim$X, sim$Y, lags = 0:4, permutation = "phase",
                      seed = 1)
fit             # lag profile, optimal lag, per-lag and global p-values
plot(fit)       # m2 against lag, with the permutation null quantile
residuals(fit)  # per-observation residuals at the optimal lag

Report the global p-value (fit$p.global) for the optimal lag: it accounts for scanning several lags and selecting the best one, whereas the per-lag p-values do not.

Inputs can be matrices or data frames (rows = ordered time points, columns = variables) or dist objects, which are converted to principal coordinates.

Status

Under development. The method and its calibration are described in a manuscript in preparation.
